properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Fixed IVs embedded inside recorded v3.1.0 ciphertext fixtures — deliberately static so the backward-compat vectors stay byte-reproducible. Not a live configuration weakness: the production encrypt path always draws a fresh random IV (src/encrypt-with-public-key.js:52-54), and the opts.iv/opts.ephemPrivateKey escape hatch exists for deterministic tests (used at test/unit.test.js:182). IV reuse would only matter if a caller passed opts.iv for multiple encryptions.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum Keccak-256 (the pre-standard SHA-3 variant with different padding — the declared name 'SHA-3' resolves to Keccak-256 here, changeable only via the Ethereum protocol which fixes this hash). Used via ethers solidityPackedKeccak256 as the library's hash() API (src/hash.js:18), for private-key derivation from entropy (src/create-identity.js:18,21,23), as the message hash signed by sign()/recovered by recover(), and across the test suite. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-declared SHA-256 via @noble/hashes 2.4.0 (shipped runtime dependency, changeable here). Not merely declared: SHA-256 is actually consumed as the HMAC-SHA256 MAC of the ECIES envelope at src/encrypt-with-public-key.js:63 and src/decrypt-with-private-key.js:57 (those use sites are outside this object's package.json site and are filed as separate findings). Hash/MAC layer survives Grover; no PQ migration needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 is available in the shipped library surface: @noble/hashes 2.4.0 (runtime dependency, package.json:108) exports a BLAKE3 implementation. No call site found in eth-crypto's own source — the application never invokes it, but any downstream consumer of the bundle can. Recorded as shipped-library capability, changeable here by dropping/limiting the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3/Keccak capability enters the build two ways: js-sha3 0.13.0 as a devDependency (package.json:76, test-time only, not shipped) and the sha3 module of the @noble/hashes runtime dependency. In this codebase the concrete use is Ethereum Keccak-256 (see ALG-052c24b2) — the standard SHA3-256 variant itself has no direct call site. Shipped-library surface + pervasive Keccak use; no PQ action (hashes are Grover-only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same six AES-256-CBC sites as ALG-443012b9, viewed by key size: encKey = sha512(sharedSecret).slice(0,32) gives a 256-bit AES key — 128-bit quantum security under Grover, adequate. No separate remediation from the AES-CBC entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Node's node:crypto CSPRNG used by the test suite: message material (issues.test.js:51) and deterministic ECIES inputs fed through the opts API (unit.test.js:182-183). The production RNG is a different surface — @noble/hashes randomBytes for the ECIES ephemeral key/IV and ethers randomBytes for identity creation (filed as separate findings). Node's crypto.randomBytes is a CSPRNG (OS entropy source) — no weakness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Primary shipped crypto provider (changeable here): @noble/hashes 2.4.0 supplies sha256, sha512, hmac and the randomBytes/utils used directly by the ECIES implementation (src/encrypt-with-public-key.js imports @noble/hashes/sha2.js, hmac.js, utils.js; same in decrypt). Pure-JS, audited noble family; version pinned exactly (2.4.0). No known weak primitives in the used surface; SHA-2/HMAC survive Grover.
